newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai fiscal surplus in Jan after two-mth deficit.
newsitem.headline: Thai fiscal surplus in Jan after two-mth deficit.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand said on Thursday the Thai government posted a small 2.9 billion baht ($112.1 million) monthly fiscal surplus in January after rare deficits in the previous two months.
The central bank attributed the January surplus to 9.2 percent revenue growth helped by increased tax collection and cash remittances by state enteprises.
The government posted a 30.3 billion and 17.2 billion baht monthly expenditure deficit respectively in December and November after about nine years of sustained surplus.
The two-month deficits raised market concern that the government may fail to achieve its balance budget target during the 1996/1997 (October/September) fiscal year.

The central bank said a recent government decision to delay 99 billion baht spending on low priority infrastructure projects and aircraft acquisition during the current fiscal year would further help improve the fiscal position later this year.
It said spending cuts in the public sector would also narrow current account deficit this year from its level of 8.0 percent of gross domestic product in 1996.
